Interface ClientCommandHandler

All Known Implementing Classes:
CardSelectHandler, EndTurnHandler, GlobalLeaderboardHandler, SetPlayersHandler, TileSelectHandler
Functional Interface:
This is a functional interface and can therefore be used as the assignment target for a lambda expression or method reference.
@FunctionalInterface public interface ClientCommandHandler
Functional interface implementing the Command pattern to handle incoming client network requests on the server.

Implementations of this interface are responsible for decoding, validating, and executing network packets or text strings sent by a client. It acts as the direct entry point for client intents into the server architecture, bridging the network transport layer with the core game controllers.

Each handler isolates the domain logic required to process a specific message token, safely interacting with the pre-game structures (Lobby), the active gameplay coordinator (RemoteController), or responding directly back to the requesting connection channel via its dedicated network view wrapper.

  • Method Details

    • handle

      void handle(String[] args, Lobby lobby, RemoteController controller, SocketVirtualView out)
      Processes and executes the specific client request within the server runtime context.

      When the server network dispatch loop intercepts a matching command signature, it extracts the raw argument tokens and invokes this method to apply state modifications or trigger game events.

      Parameters:
      args - the raw string tokens containing command parameters, payload values, or packed identifiers
      lobby - the pre-game Lobby management context, used for handling connection steps, room setups, or matchmaking
      controller - the active session's RemoteController, used to dispatch validated gameplay inputs down to the model layer
      out - the connection-specific SocketVirtualView representing the single client who initiated the request, allowing direct synchronous feedback, error replies, or localized data pushes
